basics.name: Jennifer Posada
basics.label: PhD Student | HCI & Human-AI Interaction Researcher
basics.summary: I design AI feedback systems that help people engage with data, navigate analysis, and turn personal data into meaningful stories.

work.name: TEEM NSF Project
work.summary: Research on agentic data analytics and AI support for analytical work processes (NSF #2339674).
highlights: Led interview protocol development and implementation.
Analyzed worked products to understand agent work processes and inform AI feature design.
Designed and evaluated AI feedback features for an agentic data analytics support system.

work.name: Story Studio — AI Coaching Tool, UMBC
work.summary: NSF-funded research on AI feedback and coaching for student data storytelling (NSF #2302794 and #2302795).
highlights: Led 10+ iterative co-design workshops with domain experts, instructors, and students.
Conducted and analyzed 17+ interviews and participant observations to understand data storytelling workflows.
Applied cognitive task analysis and expert interviews to model domain knowledge and guide AI coaching and instructor summaries.
Designed and evaluated AI feedback features; published first-author findings at ACM CHI 2026.

work.name: UMBC Affective Behavior Interaction Lab
work.summary: Research and design of a health-data visualization dashboard for interpreting sensor data and sharing insights.
highlights: Led research and design for dashboard features supporting collaborative interpretation.
Facilitated 3 co-design workshops and 6 interviews.
Translated findings into recommendations for data display and annotation features.

work.name: Little Steps Daycare
work.summary: Designed digital services and improved customer-facing and operational processes.
highlights: Designed and launched a website, online billing system, and CRM to replace paper-based workflows.
Improved operational efficiency by approximately 30%.
Conducted competitive analysis and synthesized customer feedback to guide service design decisions.

volunteer.organization: UMBC DARE Lab / Digital Harbor Foundation — Rec-to-Tech
volunteer.summary: NSF-funded participatory research on equitable, technology-rich STEM learning in community recreation centers (NSF #2005502).
highlights: Conducted interviews, focus groups, and observations with underserved youth and educators.
Analyzed quantitative measures of self-efficacy, creativity, and attitudes toward STEM.
Co-authored findings published at ACM CHI 2023.

volunteer.summary: Accessible co-design research for a 3D-printed tactile navigation map with blind and low-vision university students.
highlights: Led accessible design research in a Section 508 context.
Co-authored results published at ACM ASSETS 2024 and in the Journal of Enabling Technologies.
Research focus: human-AI interaction, agentic feedback, data storytelling, and personal informatics.
